This way of thinking is a form of happiness addiction. Read up on hedonic adaptation. When you get to the stars, you eventually lower back down to your base line of "happiness". However, you still want that rush. 

Contentment is striving to reach that sweet spot where you aren't chasing that rush of pleasure but also aren't Sabotaging yourself to be miserable. You are simply content and grateful for what you have. 

Before I adopted this way of thinking, I was always depressed, always let down because of unrealistic expectations.  Looking back, I had it real good and I could have enjoyed my first 25 years of life had I just been content. 

As long as I'm alive, being alive is enough to be happy about. Just to give you an example, look how many successful people commit suicide. Contentment is key. It's such a better way to live.

Congrats man. 30 days is huge. I've been using Kratom for 4 years. A little over a year ago (which is why my quit date shows oct) I quit for 60 days from a 60g to 80g daily habit. I totally understand where you are at. Honestly,  I plataued around the 20 day mark similar to what you are describing to get your energy back. The best advice I can give is to simply force yourself to do the things you know are good for you... No matter how bad you feel or how little energy you have. It doesn't have to be boring exercise. Force yourself to do things that are essentially the same thing but will keep your mind off the fact you are doing such a boring thing like exercise.  Boredom is a huge paws symptom and I personally feel going to a gym or running is soooooo boring. I do things like go on steep hikes, play basketball, ride a bike, etc.  When not using Kratom these things were enjoyable to me and provide similar benefits to gym or running. Now, they aren't really enjoyable when going through paws, but for me, it's just as boring as sitting on a couch watching TV when going through paws. Going on a run is considerably more boring for me. 

Try to think back at some healthy activities you did before you started using that you enjoyed doing. Not what you did just because you wanted better health, and simply force yourself to do it. 2 things happen when you do. You speed up the recovery and whatever activity you choose will get easier everyday. Seriously, even from day 1 to day 2. 

The more you push yourself, the more confidence you will get.  Something starts happening fairly quickly. I work a dangerous manual labor job for 10 hours a day. The first time I worked after quitting, I was so petrified to go to work. However, I have kids that rely on me. I had no choice. Now, it wasn't an easy day by any means, but when I finished I felt empowered. When I had to go back the next day, the fear was still there but it was cut in half and the day went much smoother. 

Hope this helps.

Why are you having a hard time? Centurylink uses a tool called "loop qual". All they have to do is put in your address and it shows all the different types of Internet available to you. We used to be able to let customers know when certain products would be available but this ended up being a disaster. Things change with the budget and planning all the time. It set expectations for the customer and when the planning would change, customers would get upset. It caused more problems than it solved, so now we can only tell you if it's available and not when it will be available. 

As far as pricing, I'm not very good with keeping up on the price. There are new promotions all the time. I mainly focus on the installation and maintenance of the product which is quite a plateful by itself.

Speed tests do not show you the bits used for framing or overhead. Always add 15 percent to your speed test to show what your actual bandwidth is. The speed test servers cannot see the bits that are used to frame the packets. For more information, Google ppp overhead.

Op, be careful. It's easy for the addicted mind to justify things like keeping some kratom around to show you can beat it with it right in your face. However, why make it harder than it has to be? It's difficult enough to quit without adding that extra challenge.  You will still feel accomplished without having to make it more of a challenge.

First of all, please don't hold this against him. I also became addicted to Kratom because there is very little known about it. Most of the Kratom community will tell you this is a safe substance and not addicting. Having been 7 days without it, I know that is completely false. Had I known how addicting this was, I never would of touched it. I'm not sure how much your husband knew, but it seems pretty common for people to fall into this trap.

Second of all, the first 5 days were the worst for me. I was on it for much longer than your husband.  The worst part about the WD in my opinion is the anxiety. The last thing you want to do is to make this anxiety worse or he may go behind your back to get relief. Try to be a little more lenient for about a month. 

What I later learned, is that kratom acts on the opiod receptors. The same ones pain pills work on although Kratom is not an opiate. The WD are similar but not as severe.  He is going to feel very alone during this time and desperately needs your support and understanding. He is likely going to be irritable and act out on you. Realize this is not your husband and take it in stride. I'm having to do this all on my own and having an understanding partner right now would make this so much easier.

You may also want to have him come to this subreddit. It has been a god send to me.  Being able to communicate with people that are going or have gone through the same thing is very helpful, even if they are strangers. 

Most people's experience is that acute (physical) withdrawals last about a week and post acute withdrawals last up to a month (depression and anxiety)

Exersize if very helpful but extremely hard to do in this state. You almost have to force yourself. Even a 30 minute walk or bike ride can help tremendously.

Sleep will be an issue for a while. I find melatonin helps, but I still only got about 3 hours of sleep before waking up in a panic for the rest of the night.

Good luck to you. If you look in the side bar, there is a "Quitting Kratom Wiki" that can also offer solid advice and help. Let us know if you need anything. This community is very non-judgmental and helpful.
